title: Problem Representation & Decomposition
description: Study specify goals and constraints, decompose with intermediate checks, state spaces and search, and symbolic constraints and representations. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Specify goals and constraints
lessons.description: List known constraints and identify which conclusion depends on missing information.
lessons.conceptOverview: Reasoning begins by identifying the desired output, available facts and constraints. Separate assumptions from evidence so a solution can be checked against the actual problem rather than an imagined one.
lessons.whyItMatters: Explicit assumptions make a solution auditable.

lessons.title: Decompose with intermediate checks
lessons.description: Define checks for input units, intermediate totals and final constraints.
lessons.conceptOverview: Break a problem into subproblems whose outputs can be independently verified. Decomposition helps only when dependencies are preserved and intermediate errors do not pass unchecked.
lessons.whyItMatters: Intermediate validation is as important as decomposition.

lessons.title: State spaces and search
lessons.description: Estimate the search size and identify a constraint that prunes invalid paths.
lessons.conceptOverview: A search problem defines states, actions, a transition rule and a goal test. Distinguish valid transitions from useful ones, and use resource limits because branching can grow exponentially.
lessons.whyItMatters: Search requires explicit transitions and bounded exploration.

lessons.title: Symbolic constraints and representations
lessons.description: Compare the natural-language rule with its formal expression.
lessons.conceptOverview: Represent some tasks with equations, logical constraints or structured data instead of relying solely on prose. A formal representation enables mechanical checking but still depends on a faithful translation.
lessons.whyItMatters: Formal checks validate the encoded problem, which must match the intended one.
